Documentary data have been gleaned from the original charter, the Biennial Report of the Secretary of State, 1879-1883, The Official Register of State and County Officers, and other official documents. Maps have identified the early Fannin County deed records, the charter of the Platonian Literary Society has been preserved, photographs show the Arts diploma issued in 1887, and two diplomas of years 1889 and 1890.

Books, as source material for this study, have been of very little value except for a book of biographical notes, pictorial Souvenir of Texas, published in 1889, and Carter's History of Fannin County. The lack of Texas history books of value made necessary an extended use of newspaper files and social foundation upon which this institution was built, a brief sketch of its origin, the list of known trustees and faculty members of the College. Other books have served as comparative data only.

ORGANIZATION OF THE MATERIAL

The skeleton framework of an historical study, of course, is the chronological account; in this case the natural gain of interest in the study suggested that the organization and operation of the College, on the one hand, the social life and customs of the time, on the other, should each serve their respective purposes. Chapter VIII is devoted to this point, and the formation of an ex-students' association to preserve its tradition made itself more accessible to make itself more readily to organization on the basis of nature of subject matter than to division into chronological periods. Chapter II therefore describes the locale of Savoy as a field for educational enterprise. It relates as its setting the early Fannin County history, its growth in population and its educational development. The end of the narrative is marked by the additional comments on the trustees and faculty members of The Savoy Male and Female College.
